claim:
For every \(0<w<1\), let \(X_w=(\mathbb R^2,N_w)\) be the real Banach plane with
\[
N_w(u,v)=\max\!\left\{|u|,|v|,\frac{|u|+|v|}{1+w}\right\}.
\]
For \(r>0\), define its radial retraction onto the closed radius-\(r\) ball by
\[
R_{w,r}(x)=\frac{x}{\max\{1,N_w(x)/r\}}.
\]
Then the *optimal global Lipschitz constant* in the norm \(N_w\), independent of \(r>0\), is
\[
\operatorname{Lip}(R_{w,r})=k(X_w)
=\max\left\{1+w^2,\frac{2(1+w^2)}{(1+w)^2}\right\}
=\begin{cases}
\dfrac{2(1+w^2)}{(1+w)^2},&0<w\le\sqrt2-1,\\[3pt]
1+w^2,&\sqrt2-1\le w<1.
\end{cases}
\]
The profile has exactly one minimizer, \(w=\sqrt2-1\), the regular-octagonal member, where
\[
\min_{0<w<1}k(X_w)=4-2\sqrt2.
\]
Thus the universal radial bound \(2\) improves strictly for every \(0<w<1\), while the constant tends to \(2\) at both endpoints. Sharpness on each branch is witnessed by exterior derivatives approaching one of the two kinds of octagonal vertices, with common extremal input direction \((-w,1)\).
integrity: Analytic proof based on the derivative of the radial map in two facet types, convexity of operator norms along each edge, and exact vertex norms. Boundary segments are handled by limits and continuity. The sharp lower bound comes from derivatives approaching each facet endpoint, not numerical data.
scientific_limitations: Real dimension two, canonical radial retraction only; this does not determine the optimal Lipschitz constant among all nonlinear ball retractions. Original texts of selected historical articles were unavailable; a differently named historical exact calculation remains a bibliographic risk. Historical publications with only year-level evidence were not assigned invented dates.
title: Sharp radial-retraction Lipschitz profile of the real Lorentz-predual octagonal planes
